title: Master Guide to Confusing Spanish Grammar Usage (A vs B)

a0_a2.core_difference: Ser = permanent traits, origin, identity, time, occupation. Estar = temporary states, emotions, location, ongoing actions.
a0_a2.usage_a: Use 'ser' for DOCTOR (Description, Occupation, Characteristic, Time, Origin, Relationship).
a0_a2.usage_b: Use 'estar' for PLACE (Position, Location, Action, Condition, Emotion).
a0_a2.quick_logic: How you feel and where you are, always use the verb ESTAR.
common_mistakes: ❌ Dónde es el baño? → ✓ Dónde está el baño?
a0_a2.memory_trick: For how you feel and where you are, always use ESTAR!

a0_a2.core_difference: Por = cause, reason, duration, exchange, travel route. Para = goal, destination, deadline, recipient, intended use.
a0_a2.usage_a: por expresses cause, motivation, duration ('for 2 hours'), or means of transport.
a0_a2.usage_b: para expresses destination ('to Madrid'), recipient ('for you'), deadline ('for tomorrow'), or objective ('in order to').
a0_a2.quick_logic: Looking back at cause = POR. Looking forward to purpose/destination = PARA.
common_mistakes: ❌ Trabajo por ganar dinero. → ✓ Trabajo para ganar dinero.
a0_a2.memory_trick: POR = Cause / Motive behind. PARA = Purpose / Recipient ahead.

b1_b2.core_difference: Indefinido = completed past action with clear start/end. Imperfecto = background scene, habitual past action, description, ongoing past state.
b1_b2.usage_a: Indefinido advances the story storyline with specific events (ayer, el año pasado).
b1_b2.usage_b: Imperfecto sets the stage (weather, age, feelings, repeated habits with 'siempre', 'todos los días').
examples: Cuando era niño, jugaba en el parque todos los días. (Imperfecto)
b1_b2.quick_logic: Single event / stroke = Indefinido. Background / Ongoing habit = Imperfecto.
common_mistakes: ❌ Ayer hacía sol y decidí ir al parque cuando repentinamente llovía. → ✓ ...cuando de repente llovió.
b1_b2.memory_trick: Imperfecto draws the backdrop; Indefinido shoots the action camera.
